The decision domain is '{{0_}}' and the system determines 'service eligibility and pricing tiers.' The intake does not identify the service as falling within any of the five enumerated significant-decision categories under the cited provision: financial or lending services, housing, education enrollment or opportunities, employment or independent contracting opportunities or compensation, or healthcare services. A general service-eligibility and pricing-tier determination for a consumer product that is not shown to involve financial services, lending, housing, education, employment, or healthcare does not satisfy the significant-decision test. Under the Significant-Decision Classifier rule, this assessment therefore sets triggers_significant_decision to false. {{CITE_1:cite}}

Three independent triggers under the cited risk-assessment provisions apply. First, the intake states 'Trains ADMT on PI: {{PROFILING_USE}}' — the business processes personal information intending to use it to train an ADMT; this satisfies the trigger covering processing of personal information to train an ADMT for a significant decision or to train other identified technology types. Second, the intake states 'Profiling Use: {{PROFILING_USE}}' — however, the specific profiling context (whether it involves systematic observation of consumers in their capacity as applicants, employees, students, or independent contractors, or presence at a sensitive location) is not described; these specific sub-triggers therefore cannot be confirmed. Third, if the business determines that its service falls within an enumerated significant-decision category, the trigger covering use of ADMT to make a significant decision concerning a consumer would also apply. The training-on-PI trigger is established independently of the significant-decision determination.

The cited provision defines 'significant decision' to include only decisions concerning: financial or lending services, housing, education enrollment or opportunities, employment or independent contracting opportunities or compensation, or healthcare services. The intake records fully automated operation with no human reviewer prior to the decision being applied. The human-involvement self-test fields are not answered. Under the cited provision, human involvement requires all three elements: (A) the reviewer knows how to interpret and use the technology's output; (B) the reviewer reviews the output plus any other relevant information before the decision is made; and (C) the reviewer has the authority to make or change the decision based on that analysis. Because no human reviewer is present at or before the point of decision, {{OPT_OUT_EXCEPTION}} of the three elements is satisfied. The intake describes a post-decision appeal process ('consumer may request human review within 30 days'), but an appeal that occurs after the decision is applied does not constitute human involvement as defined and does not satisfy the three-part test. Human involvement as defined is NOT present.

Three independent triggers apply under the cited provision. First, the business uses ADMT to make a decision concerning a consumer — whether or not that decision constitutes a 'significant decision' under the enumerated categories, if the service type is confirmed as financial or lending services the trigger under the ADMT-significant-decision subsection of the risk assessment provision applies. Second, and independently established on the current record, the business trains ADMT on personal information: the intake affirmatively states 'Trains ADMT on PI: {{PROFILING_USE}}.' The training-data trigger under the cited provision applies when a business processes personal information it intends to use to train an ADMT for a significant decision, or to train other specified identification or profiling technologies. This trigger is independently operative regardless of the significant-decision determination. Third, the intake confirms profiling use ('Profiling Use: {{PROFILING_USE}}'), which — depending on the capacity in which consumers are observed — may engage the systematic-observation profiling trigger. That trigger is addressed conditionally below. The risk assessment obligation is established on at least the training-data trigger.

The enumerated categories of significant decision under the cited provision are: financial or lending services, housing, education enrollment or opportunities, employment or independent contracting opportunities or compensation, and healthcare services. 'Service eligibility and pricing tiers' is not an enumerated category on its face. The intake does not identify the underlying service type — it does not specify whether the eligibility determination involves financial or lending services, housing, education, employment, or healthcare. Because the business must confirm the service type before the significant-decision trigger can be established, and advertising and general consumer subscription or commercial offerings that do not fall within the five enumerated categories are expressly excluded from the definition, this assessment conservatively treats the trigger as NOT established on the current record. {{CITE_1:cite}} The business must confirm the service type to resolve this classification.

Why We Used Automated Decision-Making for You We used the {{SYSTEM_NAME}} — an automated risk-scoring system — to evaluate your eligibility for our services and to determine the pricing tier that applies to your account. Specifically, the system analyzed your personal information, generated a numerical risk score, and applied that score against established thresholds to produce an eligibility determination and a pricing tier assignment. This automated process was the method used to make the service-eligibility and pricing decision described in this response.

How the Decision About You Was Made The risk score produced by the {{SYSTEM_NAME}} was the sole factor used to determine your service eligibility and pricing tier. No other factors independently influenced this decision. No human reviewed your application, your risk score, or the resulting eligibility and pricing determination before it was applied to you. The decision was made entirely by the automated system based on the inputs and thresholds described in this response.

What We Are Sharing and What We Are Withholding — Model Information We are providing you with the following information about how the {{SYSTEM_NAME}} produced the output that applied to you: the categories of personal information used as inputs, the risk score your information generated, the score range used by the model, how your score maps to eligibility and pricing tier thresholds, and the conceptual logic the model uses to weight different input categories. We are not disclosing the specific numerical weights, coefficients, or internal parameters assigned to individual inputs within the model. Those specific values are proprietary trade secrets, and disclosing them would harm our legitimate business interests. Withholding those specific values does not affect your ability to understand what information about you the system used, what score it produced, or why that score resulted in the eligibility and pricing outcome you received — all of that information is included in this response. If you believe this withholding is improper, you may contact us at [privacy@yourcompany.com] to discuss your request further.
